candidates.rationale: Low spill, queueing, and latency make one-size down a controlled canary candidate; absence of pressure is not proof of SLA safety.
The configured ceiling has not been used and queue pressure is low; tighten the guardrail without claiming direct savings.
Busy periods start with at most 10 concurrent queries (P95), which 1 cluster(s) carry until the autoscaler adds more; the floor moves there in one canary and its savings are an upper-bound range.

Held: the auto_stop_minutes change is applied without a canary, so it waits until its own savings can be priced. The forward DBU cost is unavailable (unpriced usage or a non-positive run rate); economics are withheld.
Migration is judged on a pre-canary cost comparison, but the current DBU cost is unavailable (unpriced usage or a non-positive run rate).

assumptions: Current configuration epoch is the decision baseline.
Forward DBU cost uses the deterministic current-epoch run-rate model.
AWS forward cost is modeled from observed current-epoch resource time and the configured regional price registry when available.
DBU cost is priced at the account's list price; negotiated discounts lower real savings in proportion.
AWS cost is priced at on-demand EC2 rates; Spot, Reserved Instances and Savings Plans are not modeled.
